The two paradigms differ most visibly in how they interpret an interval estimate
[@dobson4e, Chapter 12, p. 272].
A frequentist 95% [confidence interval](inference.qmd#def-confidence-interval)
is a random interval whose coverage probability,
over repeated samples with $\param$ held fixed,
is 0.95.
Any one realized interval either contains $\param$ or does not;
the 0.95 describes the procedure, not that interval.
A Bayesian interval estimate instead makes a probability statement
about $\param$ itself,
given the data actually observed.
